title: Wnt activation causes shell malformation in lymnaeoidean gastropods
content:
ABSTRACT
The signalling factor Wnt has recently been discovered to have a role in molluscan shell growth, but knowledge of it has been limited to the helicospiral species Lymnaea stagnalis. Here, we performed Wnt activation experiments to see whether the roles of Wnt signalling are conserved in the shell growth mechanisms of other lymnaeoidean species, including another lymnaeid helicospiral species Pseudosuccinea columella and a planispiral species of the planorbid Biomphalaria glabrata. Our results confirmed that a similar control mechanism using Wnt is indeed conserved in the shell growth of those species, which, upon manipulation, showed two types of shell malformations, namely cap-shaped malformation (Cap) and compressed malformation (Com), both in dose- and developmental stage-dependent manners. We analysed the morphologies of those malformations by a theoretical approach using the growing tube model, demonstrating that the Cap shells have significantly larger values for expansion (E) and that the Com shells show significantly larger values for both E and torsion (T), with no significant changes in curvature (C). The patterns in parameter changes brought about by the Wnt activation experiments are common not only between the two species examined in this study, but in L. stagnalis as well, suggesting that the roles of Wnt in shell growth could be conserved in even wider ranges of molluscan taxa.
